scenario: A btrfs mount whose source resolves to a device basename that no uuid under /sys/fs/btrfs lists, so the filesystem-to-device mapping fails and the quota state is unknown rather than enabled or disabled.

fixture.mountinfo:
23 28 0:21 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:12 - proc proc rw
28 1 0:30 /@root / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=256,subvol=/@root
30 28 259:1 / /tmp rw,relatime shared:1 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,noquota
36 28 0:44 /@vault /srv/data rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/vault rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=256,subvol=/@vault

rationale: Contract table row: 'btrfs | zero or several uuids list the device | unknown | n/a | btrfs_device_unmapped'. The covering mount for /srv/data/store has source /dev/mapper/vault, which device_links resolves to the device basename dm-9; btrfs_sysfs contains two uuids, one listing dm-0 and one listing dm-1, so zero uuids list dm-9 -> quota_state unknown, enforcement n/a, basis btrfs_device_unmapped. Mount resolution rule: candidate mounts are those whose mount point equals the path realpath, is '/', or is the realpath prefix followed by '/'; the longest mount point wins, so /srv/data is chosen and the btrfs /dev/mapper/root line mounted at '/' is not chosen for this path. Device-check rule: for btrfs a major:minor mismatch is expected (per-subvolume anonymous st_dev, S081) and is recorded as device_check btrfs_subvolume_skipped instead of device_mismatch, so the btrfs quota row still applies; this is corroborated by the frozen real control frozen/c2-expected-real.json, where the btrfs fleet root (mount 0:30, st_dev 0:57) carries basis btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent rather than device_mismatch. Verdict precedence: no path is enabled and one path is unknown -> exit 2, finding_id QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN. The second uuid carries qgroups true with mode 'squota' and a device that is not dm-9: neither the qgroups state nor the mode of an unrelated uuid may leak into this path, whose btrfs_qgroups_mode is null because no uuid maps to dm-9. The xfs /tmp line (noquota) and the /proc line are inert realism and are not relied upon; they exist so a parser that ignores the covering mount or scans all lines cannot pass by accident. Mountinfo lines are parsed per proc.rst 3.5 (S082): fields 1-6, optional fields up to the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and super options; 'shared:N' optional fields appear on three lines, so a parser assuming a fixed field count is caught. The mountinfo text ends with a newline because a real /proc/self/mountinfo does; a trailing newline is not an unparseable line.
